messages:
Alex: quick heads-up — canary for m-5243 shows a 8-12% p95 decode latency regression for the int8 model family. Not massive but consistent across 3 clusters.
Maya: ugh. where is the perf delta coming from? CPU or GPU?
Alex: GPU-side tokens are fine, but the runtime trace shows extra memcpy + serialization spikes during kv-cache hits. nvtx shows a new region around 'prefetcher:throttle' introduced in 9f3b2a.
Priya: can you paste the trace snippet?
Alex: pasted below (truncated):
```
[GPU timeline] kernel:decode  0.9ms -> 0.92ms
[GPU timeline] memcpy H2D   0.05ms -> 0.3ms   <-- new
[Runtime] prefetcher:throttle sleep 0.2ms on kv-hit
[KV] kv_get (hot) 0.2ms -> 0.45ms
```
Tom: that extra H2D memcpy on hot KV hits smells like an unintended copy-for-quantization-path. Wasn't there a change to make prefetcher copy cached kvs into a pinned buffer to reduce page faults?
Maya: yes, commit 9f3b2a added a pinned-buffer copy and a throttler so heavy A/B traffic doesn't starve the service. The goal was to protect overall throughput, but we probably regressed tail latency for short sequences.
Priya: did CI perf catch this? I thought our pre-merge benchmarks run int8 workloads.
Alex: CI perf did flag a small regression on the runner that had long sequences, but it was below threshold so merge proceeded. Canary exposed this because most traffic is short-chat bursts: many kv hits + tiny decode loops.
Tom: can we bisect to confirm 9f3b2a is the culprit?
Alex: did a quick bisect across the canary builds this morning. Reverted that single hunk and p95 returns to baseline. Files changed: runtime/prefetcher.{cc,h}. The diff had this chunk:
```
// new prefetch copy on kv-hit
if (use_prefetch_copy) {
  pinned_buf = allocate_pinned(size);
  memcpy(pinned_buf, src, size);
  enqueue_h2d(pinned_buf, size);
  throttler.sleep_if_needed();
}
```
Maya: aha. allocate_pinned + memcpy on every kv-hit is expensive for short sequences. For long sequences amortizes, but for chat it's a regression.
Priya: we need to decide: revert entirely or gate behind heuristics. Revert is fastest for release rollback.
Tom: another option: make prefetch use zero-copy on hot keys (map GPU-accessible host mem) and only do pinned-copy for cold keys or big tensors. Also avoid throttler.sleep on the fast-path.
Alex: agree. Ops note: this is blocking canary rollout 0.6 -> 0.7 for int8 tier. Current mitigation is to stop the canary and roll back to m-5238 (previous).
Maya: I pushed a tiny patch that disables the pinned copy by default and leaves the throttler in place for long workloads. Patch: runtime/prefetcher: flip flag default to false.
Priya: can we run a narrow canary of that patch on one region?
Alex: kicked off a region canary (eu-west-1) build 2391234599 with the flag off. infra-bot: canary creation logs: job/2391234599 started; 3 instances; metrics sink hooked.
canary-bot: initial 10k requests done — p95 improved from 420ms -> 380ms on int8 decode in eu-west-1 (baseline 375ms).
Tom: that's promising. We should still follow up with a proper fix: heuristics to avoid memcpy when seq_len < 64 and kv-hit rate > 80%. Also prefer cudaHostAllocMapped to avoid copy for hot keys.
Maya: filed an issue: runtime#1426 with the suggested heuristics and perf targets. I'll assign to Priya for a proper patch.
Priya: I'll prototype zero-copy mapping + fallback pinned-copy for cold keys. Also add a microbenchmark harness for short-seq kv-hit loops so CI will catch this class of regression.
Alex: good plan. For the interim let's revert 9f3b2a from canary and push patch to prevent accidental re-enable. Ops: can we tag the offending commit in release notes so on-call knows root cause?
Maya: added note to release/blockers doc and pinged on-call.
Alex: thanks — leaving this thread open until patch lands and we get green canary across regions.
canary-bot: eu-west-1 canary (2391234599) rolled out rollback to baseline image at 2391234680; metrics stable.
Priya: working on prototype now, will post perf runs in this thread.
Tom: also add a non-regression test in perf CI for sequences < 64 tokens with high KV hit ratio. That caught nothing because our short-seq harness was accidentally disabled last month.
Alex: noted. thanks everyone.
Maya: :thumbsup:
